title: Team CI health roster
description: Per-owning-team rollup of the CI test surfaces each team owns, over a window (date_from default -14d, maximum 30 days). It reads the same per-run evidence as engineering-analytics-flaky-tests and means the same thing by flaky: flaky_test_count is owned tests one commit was seen both failing and passing in the window (a re-run attempt went green, or an in-job retry recovered it), regression_test_count is owned tests that failed with no such proof and still hit min_failed_prs distinct PRs or master, and failed_run_count, same_commit_recovery_run_count and quarantined_failed_run_count count distinct CI runs across the team's owned tests, so one run with many failing tests counts once. A CI setup break excludes every trial of the attempt, not only its failures: a run attempt whose tests errored in three or more jobs or for three or more owning teams, or a job attempt with 100 or more distinct failed or errored tests. Each has an equal-length previous-window twin (*_prior) for honest deltas. Use this for "which team owns the flakiest surfaces right now" and to route a flaky-test or CI Signal to its owning team. Ownership is stamped on the spans at CI emission time from the repo's ownership map (the distributed owners.yaml files); spans without a stamp aggregate under the literal team 'unowned' (a nonempty 'unowned' row means ownership gaps, not a real team), and a re-stamped test lands under its latest owner only. Each row also carries test_file_count (the daily owners.yaml census denominator, with a window-start twin) and merged_pr_count (merged PRs by the team's members, bots excluded); teams with census counts but no CI signal appear with zero signal counts and a null last_seen_at. Teams are organizational owners of code surfaces, never authors. Read all counts as absolute signal, never rates: fast passing runs are not emitted, so there is no honest denominator.

Teams are organizational owners of code surfaces, never authors. Counts are absolute, never rates: CI emits every failure but omits ordinary passing spans, so there is no execution denominator. 'suspected_regression' means no recovery was recorded in this data, not that the test never flakes.

typeDocumentation.effectiveDescription: Window start: relative ('-14d', '-7d') or ISO8601. Defaults to -14d; the window may span at most 30 days. An equal-length prior window is scanned for the *_prior twins; near the 30-day ceiling that prior window can reach past Traces retention, deflating *_prior counts and overstating deltas.
